chunk_findings.detail: The generated worker script does `p.start(); p.join(120); sys.exit(p.exitcode)`. If the spawned process has not finished when `join(120)` returns, `p.exitcode` is `None`, and `sys.exit(None)` terminates the interpreter with status **0** (CPython treats `SystemExit(None)` as success). The subprocess therefore returns 0, and `test_a_spawn_worker_with_the_repo_root_first_imports_the_load_test_module` passes even though the worker never completed: a worker that *deadlocks* while importing the module (e.g. a module-level lock/import cycle in `ddflow`, the exact class of failure the pre-flight helper in `test_mcp_load.py` is written to distinguish from a "deadlock signature") is silently reported as success rather than failure. A concrete demonstration: replace the target's import path with one that blocks in `sys.modules` import (or simply insert `time.sleep(9999)` in `test_mcp_load`'s module body) — `join(120)` returns with `exitcode is None`, `sys.exit(None)` yields 0, and the test's `assert p.returncode == 0` passes instead of failing. Checking `if p.exitcode is None: sys.exit("worker did not finish")` (or asserting `p.exitcode == 0` inside the script) would make the statement truthful.

The AI to MCP communication timeouts due to very long time of what the review command is taking. We should investigate in two directions - how to make the reviews fast and linear with the code growth and still accurate, and separately could MCP starts the commands as subprocesses and continue keeping and reporting to the agent (if that is possible and MCP can initiate communication to the agent) or ask for it to poll so the AI would know when the task is completed. Separately, if the MCP is remote or within docker, should it tell (for the task for the remote MCP investigation) tell to the agent which commands to execute (maybe clone ddflow locally), instead of directly relying on the MCP to execute the commands? This way even MCP without filesystem access would be able to manage a project? Should this be part of the remote MCP investigation?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-19: reviews time out the agent<->MCP call; make them fast, LINEAR with code growth, and still accurate. Measured so far (coordinator, 2026-10-19): DeepSeek chunk reviews take 4-45 min; one chunk consumed all 64000 tokens on reasoning with no answer (critic TRUNCATED, recorded unavailable); a roborev review is a kilo agent loop of 5-47 model calls re-sending ~80k tokens each; moving roborev to the idle Pro host + a budget prompt took the same three reviews from 9-14.5 min to 1-2 min (DX-roborev-speed). Questions to answer with probes, not opinion: (1) cost model: time and tokens vs diff size for chunked vs whole-diff vs delta rounds; where is it super-linear (reasoning blow-up, re-sent context, serial chunks)? (2) parallel chunks with a bounded fan-out and per-chunk token cap; split-on-truncate (fix-B587e607ad9); reasoning-effort/temperature per gate; (3) review only what changed since the last reviewed head (delta) and only what a risk tier needs (D-phase-review); (4) a cheap prefilter (lint/types/tests-reach) so the model sees only the residual; (5) caching of the shared prompt prefix (vLLM prefix cache already 85-92%); (6) accuracy: for each lever, re-run the corpus of past confirmed findings (SE-eval-harness) and report recall/precision so speed is never bought with misses. Deliver: a cost model, the levers ranked by gain per accuracy lost, and follow-up tasks. Falsifier: time is already linear in diff size and the delay is queueing/host load only.
data.title: Reviews that stay fast and linear as the code grows, and still accurate: measure, model and propose

data.body: Operator 2026-10-19: agent<->MCP calls time out because review/gate commands take too long. Questions: (1) can the MCP server start the command as a subprocess/detached job (ddflow job run exists), keep running after the call returns, and report later? (2) can the SERVER initiate communication to the agent: MCP progress notifications (do they reset the client's request timeout?), notifications/message logging, resource-updated subscriptions, sampling/elicitation, the 2026-07-28 revision's tasks extension; which of these do Claude Code, Kilo, opencode, Codex, Gemini CLI actually surface to the model, and can any WAKE an idle agent? Probe each client, do not assume. (3) if push is not possible: the polling contract: a run handle returned within N seconds (configurable), ddflow_run_status/ddflow_wait with a bounded long-poll, a 'next poll in X s' hint and the elapsed/ETA, so the agent knows when it completed; idempotent retries by deterministic run key. (4) which tools get it first: review, gate run (DX-gate-run-detach), ci, merge, roborev standards (B-roborev-async-standards). Reuse P-remote.runs, DX-gate-run-detach, the job engine and DX-long-op-renew; do not build a second process manager. Deliver: a client capability matrix with probe output, a recommended contract, and the order of tasks. Falsifier: a client keeps a call alive while progress notifications arrive, so the only fix needed is to emit them.
data.title: MCP long operations: server-held subprocess, progress, push to the agent or poll; what each client actually supports

data.body: Operator 2026-10-19, part of the remote MCP investigation: if the MCP server is remote or in docker it cannot run git, tests or reviews on the project. Should it instead TELL the agent which commands to execute (and the agent may clone/install ddflow locally), so even a server without filesystem access can manage a project? Prior art in this repo: R14 (docs/RESEARCH.md) REFUTED delegating file I/O to the agent over MCP primitives (roots/list gives file:// URIs; sampling and elicitation are not file access) and R-storage-seam/P-storage keep a server that needs no client filesystem via a storage seam; D-dispatch-modes already has a propose-only mode. This is different: plain instructions in tool results, executed by the agent's own shell. Questions: (1) a 'client-exec' mode where each ddflow tool returns {commands:[...], then: 'call ddflow_X with the result'} for the parts that need the working tree (worktree create, gate/test runs, git merge), while the log/queue/lease/decision state stays server-side; (2) how results come back (the agent calls ddflow_record/gate_record with captured output; evidence and exit codes are agent-reported, so trust labels and the unavailable-never-passed rules must hold); (3) the thin client: a local ddflow CLI pointed at the remote server (P-remote.serve) vs the agent running raw commands; (4) failure modes: an agent that skips or fakes a step, partial execution, secrets in commands, Windows/mac paths; (5) which tools stay server-only. Probe with a fake agent on a server container that has no repo mount. Deliver: go/no-go, the contract, and tasks. Falsifier: the agent-reported evidence cannot be made verifiable enough for the gates that D-everything-gated requires.
data.title: Remote or containerised MCP with no filesystem access: the server returns the commands for the agent to run, a thin local clone does the work

data.body: Operator 2026-10-19: review commands exceed the agent<->MCP call timeout (a review is 4-45 min on the LAN hosts) so agents start them as background shell processes and poll output files by hand. Interim, concrete fix that does not wait for the research (RM-long-ops-research, P-remote.runs): ddflow review gets --detach (and the MCP tool a [review].sync_wait_s knob, default well under the client timeout): start the review as a ddflow job (ddflow job run, survives the caller), return {run key, log path, started_at, poll_after_s}, record gate.started, keep the lease renewed (DX-long-op-renew), and record the outcome when it ends. A retry with the same item+head joins the same run (idempotent key). Poll with the existing wait/status surface (bounded long-poll). Regression test: a review that outlasts sync_wait_s returns a handle and a later poll yields the recorded outcome; a second identical call joins, not duplicates. Reuse the job engine and DX-gate-run-detach's runner; do not add a process manager. Order: share the detach runner with DX-gate-run-detach.
data.title: ddflow_review and ddflow review --detach: return a run handle, the review keeps running, poll for the result

chunk_findings.detail: The added pre-flight does not fix the actual import collision; it only converts the eventual deadlock into a deterministic failure. In the affected CI layout, `test_mcp_load.py` still inserts the repo root at `sys.path[0]` and this hunk does not change the module’s `from conftest import run_cli`. So `_preflight_spawn_import(ctx)` spawns `_noop`, the child imports `test_mcp_load`, `conftest` again resolves to the repository-root `conftest.py` (which still lacks `run_cli`), `proc.exitcode != 0` becomes true, and the new `pytest.fail` fires. The bug’s root cause remains; the CI scenario still cannot run `_pool_map` successfully.
